conviction_note: Q3 releases four weeks after the company already cut FY26 Adjusted EBITDA guidance from +10-14% FXN to 'broadly stable' (6-K 2026-10-22), and the stock fell 16.6% from 5.41 to 4.51 over the next six sessions. The question for this print is therefore whether quantifying the Colombian payor contract makes the guide worse than 'broadly stable', not whether Q3 beats a stale consensus. Strong Q3 volume KPIs, a reset bar and the post-cut drawdown roughly offset the open contract review, the Oncosalud membership dip and Peru penalties. The findings sum to +0.4 and the scaled number is -0.1 (p_up 49 x abs 5.0); the two agree that this is close to a non-result, and the 0.5-point gap is the small weight p_up puts on the serial-disappointment pattern (Q1 miss, Q2 miss, October cut).

EPS: $0.27 (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-11-10, https://finviz.com/news/420639/aunas-third-quarter-must-prove-margin-recovery-can-catch-up-with-solid-revenue). That figure looks stale from before the cut: it sits 35% above Q3'25's $0.20, while the company now guides FY Adjusted EBITDA flat. FXEmpire's 'PEN 0.85' conflicts on currency. Adjusted EBITDA, the line this stock trades on: no sourced Q3 consensus. The real bar is the company's 2026-10-22 guide, FY26 Adjusted EBITDA 'broadly stable YoY' against FY25 S/917m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1799207/000095010326015991/dp255384_ex9901.htm). Because the EBITDA bar is unsourced, every finding is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is a revenue read.

FY26 Adjusted EBITDA 'broadly stable year over year', cut from +10-14% FXN on 2026-10-22, with the payor-contract impact 'still under review, details on the Q3 call'. Capex ~4% of revenue. next_guide.basis: The cut came 22 days after quarter end, when Q3 was largely closed, so Q3 itself should match it. Flat FY EBITDA needs H2 of about S/473m (S/917m less H1 S/444m) against H2'25 S/452m, about +5% YoY, which Mexico's Q3 volume recovery makes reachable. The company explicitly left the contract review open, though, so a modest further trim (a slight decline) is the main risk.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 Auna cut FY26 Adjusted EBITDA from +10-14% FXN growth (low end, excluding Peru penalties) to 'broadly stable YoY'. It blamed 'an unexpected high incidence of advanced-stage cancer cases' under a Colombian payor contract and said it is 'completing its review of the implications... details on the Q3 call'. So the FY EBITDA guide is not final, and this release is where it gets formalised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The cut itself: -7.0% on 2026-10-22, -16.6% by 2026-10-30. Q4'25, the first FY guide: +8.33. Q1'26 margin miss with guidance kept: -7.79. Q2'26 'low end' guide: +0.18.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction of the cut is priced (-17%). The size of the contract hit and whether 'broadly stable' becomes a decline are not public. If the market expected a further cut, the stock would still be falling into the print; instead it has sat flat at 4.50-4.71 for 12 sessions.
findings.independence: Quartr's Investor Day summary carries the same wording (https://quartr.com/companies/auna-sa_16604). Same underlying document, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: The guide was reset 22 days after the 30 September quarter end, when management had most of Q3 in hand, so the reported Q3 Adjusted EBITDA should sit inside the new 'broadly stable' frame. Flat FY (about S/917m) less H1 S/444m (S/217m + S/227m) leaves H2 about S/473m, against H2'25 S/452m (Q3'25 S/232m + Q4'25 S/220m): about +5% YoY, not the roughly +25% the original low end needed. The risk of a fresh Q3 surprise is lower than on the last three prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EBITDA disappointed on Q1'26 (-7.79) and Q2'26 (+0.18, already flagged by the Q1 trend). This is the first print after a pre-announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stale $0.27 EPS consensus (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-10) shows the aggregated street number has not been rebased, so a mechanical 'miss' headline is likely even if Q3 lands inside the company's frame. FY25 S/917m and quarterly figures are from https://www.itiger.com/news/2618969395 (2026-03-10) and https://www.itiger.com/hant/news/2585168669 (Q3'25, 2025-11-20).
findings.independence: Shares the 2026-10-22 6-K with the previous finding, read for the opposite risk. The H1 figures come from the Q2 release (https://s203.q4cdn.com/408268012/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Auna_2Q26-Earnings_Release.pdf).

findings.finding: Q3'26 KPIs released 2026-10-15 show volume growth in all three markets. Mexico surgeries 5,807 (+12.2% YoY, +11.8% QoQ), utilisation 41.1% (+2.0pp). Peru surgeries 6,107 (+21.3% YoY), utilisation 89.2%. Colombia surgeries 12,018 (+7.2% YoY), protected lives 3.21m (+6.0%). This supports revenue at or above the ~S/1,245m consensus and the 'continued strong recovery in Mexico' the company cited.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue has beaten all year (Q1'26 +10% FXN, Q2'26 +9% FXN), and the stock moved -7.79 and +0.18 on those prints: revenue beats are not paid here.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public a month ago, and the stock rose from 5.30 to 5.43 before the cut. It is filed because it bounds the revenue line, which consensus already expects to be strong.
findings.independence: Oct 22 6-K: 'continued strong recovery in Mexico during the second half' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1799207/000095010326015991/dp255384_ex9901.htm).

findings.finding: Oncosalud Peru plan memberships fell to 1,441,794 at the end of Q3'26 from 1,472,019 at the end of Q2'26 (-2.1% QoQ, about 30k members), the first sequential decline in the five quarters shown; they are still +3.3% YoY. Oncosalud is about 25% of revenue at about S/63/member/month.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior isolated reaction to a membership decline. Membership growth was always a cited positive (+6% in Q2'26).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a KPI-table line no headline carried. The Q2 release cited 6% membership growth and a new 7,000-member SEDAPAL B2B account. Lost members worth about S/5-6m of quarterly revenue are small, but a churn signal could show on the call as weaker Q4 Oncosalud revenue or a lower MLR benefit.
findings.independence: Q2 release membership 1,472k (https://s203.q4cdn.com/408268012/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Auna_2Q26-Earnings_Release.pdf). Net of the rest: Peru healthcare-services volumes grew (surgeries +21% YoY), which offsets most of it.

findings.finding: Peru billing penalties on prior-year receivables hit Q1 and Q2'26 and are excluded from the adjusted guide. The CFO said on the Q2 call that 'current negotiations related to prior periods do remain open' and that they would be finalised 'during this year', so Q3 or Q4 can carry another penalty charge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Penalties first hit Q1'26 (-7.79) and were repeated in Q2'26 (+0.18).
findings.why_not_priced: Known and excluded from the guide. A closing settlement could read either way: a final charge (negative) or 'cleaned out' (positive for 2027). The penalty amount has never been quantified in the company's documents.
findings.independence: The Oct 22 6-K repeats 'payor billing penalties' as the excluded item (same company source).

findings.finding: Colombia's government created a one-off ADRES credit line (Resolution 002445, 22 October 2026, about COP 500bn) for EPS to pay overdue debts to hospitals and clinics with irrevocable direct payment, and raised minimum direct payment to IPS to 90% in August. This supports Auna Colombia's collections; Colombia is 34% of revenue and 12% comes from intervened payors.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Collections and FCF have been the positive line all year (FCF +181% in Q2'26), and the stock did not pay for it (+0.18).
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. It lands on cash, receivables and leverage (the Investor Day path to 3.0x in 2027), not on EBITDA, so it is small.
findings.independence: Vanguardia 2026-10-02 on the credit-line proposal (https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2026/10/02/gobierno-propone-linea-de-credito-para-que-las-eps-paguen-deudas-pendientes/). The Q2 release welcomes the Emergency Stabilization Plan.
findings.link: Auna Colombia is a provider (IPS) paid by EPS, including Nueva EPS and other intervened payors (12% of Colombia revenue in Q2'26).

findings.finding: Management said FCF will 'exceed our original internal expectations' (Q2 release) and repeated on 2026-10-22 that FCF and leverage 'continue to evolve favorably'. Investor Day set deleveraging toward 3.0x during 2027 (from 3.6x) and possible shareholder returns in 2027-2028, so Q3 leverage below 3.6x is likely despite flat EBITDA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2'26 FCF +181% and leverage 3.6x print moved +0.18.
findings.why_not_priced: Directionally guided. The number is not out, and this name has not paid for cash lines, so it is small.
findings.independence: Quartr Investor Day summary (https://quartr.com/companies/auna-sa_16604), which is a summary of the same company material.

findings.finding: A 6-K (2026-10-27/28) carries a spin-off pro forma at 30 September 2026. It moves nearly all of Grupo Salud Auna México's subsidiaries, MXN 6.66bn of loans, derivatives and related-party balances into a new Grupo Salud Auna México Hospitales (GSAMH), leaving GSAM with MXN 0.40bn of assets. The filing discloses no purpose and no P&L effect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 4.88 to 4.74 (-2.9%) on 2026-10-28 with no other news found.
findings.why_not_priced: Its purpose (a Mexico-level financing, a partner or a sale process, or a tax reorganisation) is unexplained and may be addressed on the call. It is filed at 0 because the sign depends on an answer nobody has.

baseline_tension: No skew exists. The 20-day run-up of -14.3% (about -17.5 points against XLV) is the market already pricing the October cut, so my small positive expectations finding runs with the drawdown, not against it. Lean is essentially neutral.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the Oncosalud membership dip went from -0.4 to -0.3, because Peru healthcare-services volumes (+21% surgeries) offset it.

Lesson 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): the stale EPS consensus finding went from -0.5 to -0.4. The EBITDA bar is unsourced and the EPS bar disputed across currencies, so every finding stays capped small, as drafted.
Lesson 'reaction history from wrong events': the base rate was rebuilt from four confirmed prints (median absolute 4.9%); abs_move_pct stays at 5.0.
Lessons 3, 7 and 8 checked and left standing: no self-contradicting finding, short interest is not crowded so negatives stay, no confirmed unpriced company number on a thin name to enlarge.
